title: Rollout plan for hardware tuning profile pack (Hosted canary → Dedicated opt-in → Private guidance) + success criteria
creator: Talia Benson
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Owner: Rafael Mendes (with Sean Gallagher as SRE approver).

Context
We are enabling the versioned runtime “hardware tuning profile pack” as the default behavior in Hosted (staged), with Dedicated customers able to opt in and pin versions, and Private installs receiving clear guidance + safe defaults. This ticket defines: (1) rollout stages by deployment mode, (2) objective SLO/perf gates, (3) rollback/kill-switch semantics and on-call runbook hooks, and (4) success criteria to declare rollout complete.

Rollout goals
- Validate no statistically meaningful regression in tail latency under mixed workloads (focus p99/p99.9) during staged rollout.
- Validate error-rate stability (5xx, timeouts, OOM, admission-control rejects) and predictable throughput.
- Ensure rollback is safe, fast, auditable, and well understood by on-call.
- Ensure Dedicated customers have a clear opt-in path and can pin/rollback profile versions with guardrails.
- Ensure Private installs can select supported defaults for their SKU/driver/CUDA combination, and can override safely with documented constraints.

Non-goals
- Per-customer bespoke tuning beyond documented override surfaces.
- Any changes to external SLAs (handled by Product/Legal).

Definitions
- “Profile pack enabled”: runtime selects and applies profile(s) from the versioned profile pack artifact; runtime exports profile_id/profile_version tags and logs active knob summary at startup.
- “Default-on”: profile pack enabled for all Hosted traffic on supported SKUs; Dedicated remains customer-controlled (opt-in/pin) by default; Private guidance published.

Rollout stages (Hosted)
Stage 0 — Pre-flight (internal only)
- Preconditions:
  - profile_id/profile_version present in latency histograms and request logs (ENG-4931).
  - scheduler_queue_ms and kernel_choice metrics visible on dashboards (ENG-4931).
  - /health and debug endpoints include profile_version and detected SKU (PR-25014).
  - perf-canary checks active on default-profile changes (ENG-4930).
- Gate to proceed: dashboards show stable baseline for 24h on current default (non-profile-pack).

Stage 1 — Hosted canary 1%
- Cohort: 1% of Hosted traffic in 1 region (choose lowest business risk + representative traffic mix), restricted to H100 PCIe pools only initially.
- Enable mechanism: feature flag from PR-24979; kill-switch available to disable pack selection and revert to previous defaults.
- Duration: 24h minimum.
- Blockers (rollback triggers):
  - p99 end-to-end latency regression > 5% vs matched control for same model/workload bucket for > 30 min.
  - p99.9 latency regression > 8% for > 15 min.
  - 5xx error rate +0.10% absolute sustained for > 15 min (or per SRE guardrail doc).
  - OOM/restarts increase (OOM counter or container restart rate > 2x baseline in canary cohort).
  - kernel_fallback_rate > 1% sustained for > 30 min on stable workloads (excluding explicitly documented expected behavior buckets).
- Required checks during Stage 1:
  - “Runtime Profiles” overview: adoption by profile_id, p95/p99 by profile.
  - Queueing vs compute breakdown: scheduler_queue_ms distribution.
  - GPU memory headroom + fragmentation estimate trends (if available).
  - Top N models by traffic: verify per-model deltas aren’t hiding behind aggregate improvement.

Stage 2 — Hosted canary 10% (multi-region)
- Cohort: 10% traffic across 2 regions; include H100 SXM pools if available; include small L40S cohort only if stable results on H100.
- Duration: 48h minimum (to capture weekday/weekend patterns if possible).
- Gates: same as Stage 1, plus:
  - No sustained increase in admission-control rejects > 2x baseline (profile-aware admission control must remain conservative).
  - P95 throughput stability: tokens/sec per GPU not worse than -3% on steady-state benchmarks (bench-lab tags).

Stage 3 — Hosted ramp 25% → 50% → 100% on supported SKUs
- Ramp cadence: 25% (24h) → 50% (24h) → 100% (72h).
- SKU policy:
  - H100: eligible for default-on once Stage 2 passes.
  - L40S: gated separately; only ramp after L40S-specific OOM/fragmentation checks pass for 48h (see SUP-21958 learnings).
  - B200: DO NOT default-on. Require explicit profile_version pin + compatibility gate (PR-24927) until we exit early access.
- Ongoing monitoring: alerts tuned to page on-call only for severe regressions; otherwise ticket.

Hosted rollback/kill-switch semantics
- Primary rollback: disable profile pack feature flag (revert to previous runtime defaults).
- Secondary rollback: pin profile_version to last known-good in control plane (when available) for cohorts while keeping pack enabled.
- Documentation requirement: include exact command/flag location + who has permission to toggle (SRE) and audit expectations.
- Rollback SLO: regain baseline within 15 minutes (prop + restart time) after toggling.

Dedicated rollout plan (opt-in)
- Default stance: Dedicated customers remain opt-in for profile pack changes in runtime-1.22.
- Opt-in mechanism:
  - Customer can set runtime config: profile_pack.enabled=true and (recommended) profile_version pin.
  - Guardrails: refuse unsafe combinations (unsupported driver/CUDA for SKU; prohibited memory headroom settings).
  - Audit: customer override recorded (see PR-24944 audit hook).
- Customer comms:
  - Provide CS/Solutions playbook: what changes, expected behavior, how to pin/rollback; link to Dedicated messaging draft (PM-881).
  - For customers with strict SLOs: recommend canary at customer level (subset of traffic / shadow).
- Success criteria for Dedicated opt-in readiness:
  - Support can answer “what profile am I on?” using debug bundle; profile_version appears in standard on-call bundle (INT-8831).
  - At least 2 internal Dedicated-like clusters run with profile pack enabled for 7 days with no P0 incident.

Private deployment guidance
- Publish guidance for Helm/private installer defaults:
  - Default: profile_pack.enabled=true for supported SKUs if compatibility gate passes; otherwise warn and require explicit selection.
  - Document required vs best-effort host settings (CPU pinning/NUMA/hugepages) by deployment mode (Private may vary).
  - Provide example values.yaml snippet and explanation of override precedence (fleet defaults vs operator override vs runtime-detected SKU).
- Hard requirements:
  - Installer warns on unsupported driver/CUDA combos and suggests supported baselines (PR-602).
  - Document how to disable pack or pin profile_version during upgrades.

Objective success criteria (declare rollout complete)
- Hosted (H100): 100% traffic on supported pools for 7 consecutive days, meeting gates:
  - No statistically significant p99 regression (>5%) for top 10 models by traffic (per workload bucket).
  - No increase in overall 5xx rate (>0.05% absolute) attributable to profile pack.
  - No net increase in OOM/restarts; fragmentation signals stable or improved.
- Hosted (L40S): 100% traffic on L40S pools for 7 consecutive days with:
  - OOM rate not worse than baseline; concurrency caps honored; stable p99.
- Dedicated: opt-in path documented; support playbook published; at least 2 successful customer opt-ins (or internal “customer zero”) without rollback.
- Private: docs published + reviewed by SRE/Infra; installer warnings validated in a dry-run environment; helm chart exposes relevant values with safe defaults.

Open questions
1) Who owns final approval to progress from Stage 2 → Stage 3: SRE (Sean) vs Runtime sponsor (Mateo)? Proposed: SRE owns go/no-go with Runtime signoff.
2) Exact thresholds for kernel_fallback_rate alerting by SKU/workload bucket (Allison to confirm in dashboard spec).
3) Can we standardize canary cohort selection (region/model mix) as a config artifact rather than ad-hoc?

Acceptance criteria
- A written rollout checklist exists for Hosted/Dedicated/Private including gates, dashboards, rollback steps, and comms template.
- SRE guardrail numbers are copied into the checklist (no “TBD” in gating).
- Dedicated/Private guidance includes pin/rollback instructions and compatibility warnings.
- Go/no-go decision log is captured for enabling default-on in Hosted.

Notes from recent rollout learning
- We saw a small p99 regression during early canary when batching defaults were too aggressive (see PR-24988). The plan must explicitly call out that any p99 regression sustained > 30 min triggers rollback and requires a follow-up benchmark-lab rerun before reattempting ramp.
